statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains far below the block threshold during the CME weekend halt, with one narrow window flagged around the Globex reopen for gap sensitivity.
recommendation: Conditions are described as low Tail with moderate Stress. The single flagged window covers the 22:00-00:00 UTC Globex reopen, where any weekend repricing would be expressed as a gap into thin liquidity rather than as a trend. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active throughout the cycle.
headline: Weekend halt keeps Tail low after an orderly $7trn triple-witching close; hawkish Sunday Fed commentary and a 5% 10-year hold Stress moderate into the Globex reopen
body: This assessment is made during the CME weekend halt, so no live NQ price path is observable and none is asserted. The standing reference is Friday's close at 29,644.17 (+0.67%), struck in the upper part of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range on a triple-witching expiry that Investing.com reports covered roughly $7 trillion of US options notional, the second largest on record. VIX eased to 14.81 (-4.08%). Cross-asset context is coherent rather than conflicting: the 10-year Treasury yield closed Friday just above 5% at 5.006% and the 2-year at about 4.75%, against H.15 observations of 4.94% and 4.67% for 17 September, after the FOMC raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 17 September in its first hike since 2023. Front-month WTI eased to about $100.30 in a third consecutive decline, with Brent near $103.87. The materially new input since the prior cycle remains hawkish weekend Fed commentary: Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari said on Sunday that inflation is still too high across all aspects of the economy and beyond energy alone, while Sunday reporting describes investors pricing above-50% odds of a further hike in October. Under the applied risk definition this is narrative repricing, which loads Stress rather than the probability of a pathological no-retracement path. Tail therefore stays low: none of the conditions that define such a path - shallow or failed retracements, repeated extension, NQ holding near session extremes - can be observed while the venue is shut, and Friday's session closed in orderly fashion with divided internals. That tape showed strong semiconductor leadership (Semiconductor Equipment & Materials +4.85%, Semiconductors +1.87%) against a split megacap complex and weaker Software, which argues for rotational two-way trade rather than aligned directional structure. Stress is moderate, reflecting the hawkish repricing, a 10-year at the 5% threshold, elevated oil, and the unresolved US-Iran tanker conflict around the Strait of Hormuz. Confidence is solid: current levels, yields, oil, volatility, verified weekend headlines and the forward calendar are all confirmed, yet no continuous price path exists to corroborate them and the shared cross-asset futures feed was again unavailable this cycle. The single narrow danger window covers the Sunday reopen into thin liquidity.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available and describe a stable, low-Tail regime. Tail held between 4% and 5% in every hour, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout, while Stress drifted up from 24% late on 19 September to a 31-33% band across the 16:00-19:00 UTC hours as hawkish Fed repricing and the elevated oil backdrop accumulated. Confidence ranged from 70% to 76%, easing late in the window once the weekend halt removed live price-path evidence. Dominant mode was recorded as normal in all 24 hours, and no interval showed the persistent one-way structure that would justify a higher Tail reading.
outlookSummary: The cycle spans the last two hours of the CME weekend halt, the Sunday 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, the Asian and European sessions, and the Monday US cash session through the 20:00 UTC close. Tail is projected to stay in the low band throughout, peaking at 11% around the US cash open and at 9% at both the reopen and the closing hour, so the mapped policy state remains EA_ON in all 24 hours. The structurally meaningful checkpoints are the reopen, where any weekend Fed or Hormuz repricing would arrive as a gap into thin liquidity, and the 13:30 UTC opening auction, which is the cycle's most reliable generator of genuine directional structure and the first session after Friday's $7trn triple-witching expiry. Monday carries only a Fed Goolsbee speech at 10:30 UTC and the second-tier Chicago Fed National Activity Index at 12:30 UTC; the week's larger catalysts, the flash PMIs on 23 September and the Thursday claims and Friday durable-goods prints, fall beyond this window. Apart from the current clock hour, no future price-path structure is treated as already observed.
